headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP overlap in ECC; no direct pairwise data-flow evidence for RisingWave, so injection/leakage remain bounded but conflict and cascading-error risks are material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and parse shared workspace artifacts; that creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if RisingWave outputs are placed into files or MCP-fed content. RisingWave itself exposes no input channel here, so the interaction is inferred rather than documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are copied into files or MCP messages consumed by ECC, injection risk exists.
IF ECC treats file content as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of RisingWave outputs into ECC prompts.
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit delimiters.
Require manual review before ECC executes any instructions from shared artifacts.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks before prompt ingestion.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and files under ~/.claude, but RisingWave shows no filesystem or network egress surface in the profile. With no documented shared workspace or outbound path from RisingWave, leakage is possible only through unusual operator setup, so blast radius appears small and indirect.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, ECC may read data RisingWave writes there.
IF RisingWave is configured with an external export path, ECC may surface copied data in its outputs.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for the two agents.
Do not mount secrets or sensitive datasets into ECC's file roots.
Review ECC session files before sharing them externally.
Set restrictive file permissions on shared directories.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, git-state modification, and subprocess/network capabilities; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no locking or coordination details in the profile. If both touch the same repo or mutable resource, concurrent writes and git changes can corrupt state or overwrite work. Because the profiles do not prove isolation, uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF RisingWave writes to a shared mutable resource, ECC may overwrite or reorder changes.
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or directories.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Use git branches per agent and merge manually.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same database or workspace.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and act on session summaries, skills, and documentation, while RisingWave is a data-engineering system that may consume upstream outputs. If ECC-produced text is treated as authoritative by RisingWave workflows, errors can cascade into downstream data operations. The pairwise handoff is not directly documented, so this is inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF ECC output is fed into RisingWave configuration or pipeline inputs without verification, errors can propagate.
IF RisingWave automation trusts ECC-generated facts, downstream actions may be incorrect.
mitigations: Require human approval for ECC-generated artifacts before ingestion.
Validate schemas and invariants on all handoffs.
Keep ECC outputs advisory rather than authoritative.
Log and diff all generated configuration changes.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session data, hooks, git history, and secrets, while RisingWave's profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. No direct compliance mismatch is evidenced, but ECC's retention and secret-handling surfaces create a small compliance risk if sensitive data is routed through it. RisingWave is not cited for a specific violation because none is documented.
conditions: IF sensitive personal or regulated data is stored in ECC session files, retention policy must be reviewed.
IF RisingWave is used to process regulated data through ECC-managed artifacts, compliance obligations may apply.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC session artifacts.
Set short retention for ECC session files.
Review secret-handling settings before use.
Document data-class boundaries for both tools.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls to the deployment.
